historical_references.reference: The river Sharavathi, also known as the Saundatti River, is a tributary that flows into the Krishna River. Its source is in the Western Ghats, and it passes through the Karnataka region in southwestern India. The name Sharavathi is derived from the Sanskrit word 'Sharabha', which refers to a mythological creature, a lion-headed man with the body of a serpent. This creature is believed to be an incarnation of Lord Shiva. The river is thus considered sacred, and is the site of numerous temples and pilgrimages.

The name Sharavathi is also mentioned in the works of the medieval poet-saint Allama Prabhu, who lived in the 16th century in the Karnataka region. He wrote extensively about the river and its beauty, and his poems have been a source of inspiration for generations of poets and musicians in the region.
